title: Kirk D. Lyons v. Western Carolina Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC answered both stated issues no, denying the challenge to Presbytery’s investigation and its finding of no strong presumption of guilt. It also held that Lyons lacked standing because he was not under Presbytery’s jurisdiction.
first_summary: Lyons challenged Presbytery’s investigation of accusations against a teaching elder, alleging that investigators failed to interview accusers, delayed excessively, and wrongly found no strong presumption of guilt. The SJC denied the complaint. BCO 31-2 prescribes due diligence and discretion, but no particular timeline or interview procedure; absent clear constitutional error, Presbytery’s factual and discretionary judgment received deference.
summary: Lyons challenged Presbytery’s investigation of accusations against a teaching elder, alleging failure to interview accusers, undue delay, and an erroneous finding of no strong presumption of guilt. The SJC denied the complaint and additionally held that Lyons lacked standing because he was not under Presbytery’s jurisdiction. The consolidated opinion explained that BCO 31-2 requires due diligence but prescribes neither interviews nor a timeline; finding no constitutional or clear factual error, it deferred to Presbytery’s judgment.

sources.supports: Case identity, Lyons’s allegations, stated issues and judgments, BCO 31-2 reasoning, deference, and Lyons-specific standing ruling.

evidence_notes.identity_and_adoption: The consolidated caption identifies Case 2009-09 as Kirk D. Lyons’s complaint against Western Carolina Presbytery (printed p. 197, line 11); the panel decision was amended by the full SJC (printed p. 207, line 274).
evidence_notes.dispute: Lyons alleged that Presbytery accepted an inadequately investigated finding of no strong presumption of guilt without hearing his evidence (printed pp. 203–204, lines 159–179).
evidence_notes.outcomes_and_reasons: The SJC answered both issues no; BCO 31-2 specifies no interviews or timeline, and the record showed no clear constitutional error overcoming deference (printed pp. 205–207, lines 195–227, 266–272).
evidence_notes.qualifications: Unlike complainants generally addressed on the merits, Lyons and Woodward were also found to lack standing because they were not under the court’s jurisdiction (printed p. 207, lines 261–264).
evidence_notes.incorporated_decisions: No decision was incorporated by reference; the opinion quotes BCO 31-2 and Ramsay only as supporting authorities (printed pp. 205–206, lines 211–245).

source_limits: The decision consolidates four complaints, so much of its merits reasoning is collective. The investigating committee’s Attachment G was absent from the record, but the operative judgment and adopted reasons are supplied.
